      <description><p>President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo</p><p>Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.</p><p>The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/08/egypt-two-trains-deadly-collision">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie</link>

      <description><p>Remains believed to have belonged to Africans or Afro-Brazilians repatriated after being flown back by diplomats </p><p>Two skulls, including that of a man believed to have taken part in Brazil’s greatest slave revolt but whose remains were taken to the United States and used in racist eugenics studies at Harvard University, were repatriated on Wednesday.</p><p>The remains had been outside Brazil since the 19th century.       <description><p>Lawyer says Britain wrong to believe in historic doctrine that crown has sovereignty over parts of oceans</p><p>Britain should not be permitted to act as a 17th-century colonial power treating the waters around the Falkland Islands as a <em>Dominium maris Britannici</em>, Argentina has told an international tribunal.</p><p>Marcelo Kohen, representing Argentina at a hearing in Hamburg, mocked Britain for apparently believing in the historic doctrine that the British crown has sovereignty over expansive parts of the oceans.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/nov/11/argentine-lawyer-mocks-uk-sovereignty-claim-in-falklands-oil-case">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/technology/live/2026/nov/13/nvidia-jensen-huang-to-testify-before-congress-live-latest-updates</link>
      <description><p>Huang’s resignation has sent shockwaves through the AI industry, after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/12/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-resigns"><strong>Full report: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO</strong></a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/12/jensen-huang-built-an-ai-kingdom-now-hes-gone-will-nvidias-ramparts-be-breached"><strong>Analysis: Jensen Huang built an AI kingdom. Now he’s gone, will Nvidia’s ramparts be breached?</strong></a></p></li></ul><p><strong>Jensen Huang is expected to testify before the US Congress in the next fortnight, after the Nvidia CEO stepped down from the multi-trillion dollar company on Thursday, plunging the chipmaker into crisis and sending shock waves across the global AI industry.</strong></p><p>House foreign affairs chair Brian Mast, a Florida Republican, told reporters on Thursday that congressional staff spoke to Nvidia on Wednesday night about a date and location for Huang’s testimony.</p><p><strong>Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday as chief executive of Nvidia after reports of extramarital affairs with <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/11/nvidia-hires-leading-us-law-firm-to-investigate-jensen-huang-relationship">an alleged Chinese spy</a> and <a href="https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/11/technology/jensen-huang-nvidia-affair.html">a company employee</a>, bookending a stunning fall from grace of one of the leading figures of the AI boom. </strong>He will be replaced on an interim basis by Nvidia’s chief financial officer, Colette Kress, until a successor is named.</p><p><strong>Shares in the chipmaker plunged by 14% when Wall Street opened, after Huang’s departure was announced and ricocheted through the global economy, before recovering to</strong> <strong>finish more than 4% lower</strong> as uncertainty about Nvidia’s future leadership troubled investors eased somewhat.</p><p><strong>US House Speaker Mike Johnson said there was ​growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China after the scandal</strong>. Lawmakers from both parties have called for tougher restrictions on China’s access to advanced AI chips, threatening access to chips that underpin China’s surging AI development.</p><p><strong>On Thursday came reports that the ousted former CEO had an intimate relationship with a second employee.</strong> The revelation, reported by Reuters, follows allegations of two other extramarital ⁠affairs that led to Jensen Huang’s dramatic resignation – one with Alice Huang, ​an alleged Chinese spy, and another with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice-president of health care. Powell has been approached for comment. On Sunday, Jensen Huang admitted he had been unfaithful to his wife, Lori, without naming anyone involved.</p><p><strong>A statement from Nvidia’s board of directors confirming Huang’s departure did not mention the spying scandal and personal conduct revelations, instead paying tribute to Huang’s “profound” contributions to the company he co-founded.</strong> “Jensen’s contributions to Nvidia are profound. Nvidia is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry,” the statement said. It added that Huang had resigned as chief executive, president and Nvidia board member “effective immediately”.</p><p><strong>Donald Trump, who had defended Huang at first as the scandal threatened to overwhelm Nvidia co-founder, quickly moved on to potential successors on Thursday, posting on social media that he should be replaced by Tim Cook, Apple’s former chief executive and current executive chair.</strong> “NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place – TIM COOK of Apple,” Trump wrote, adding: “A Legend replaces a Legend!” Nvidia’s board directors said it would consider internal and external candidates for the chief executive role, with Cook featuring among potential runners and riders before Trump’s intervention. Rene Haas, the chief executive of Arm Holdings, a UK-based chipmaker, has also been mooted, along with Lisa Su, the chief executive of the chipmaker AMD.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/live/2026/nov/13/nvidia-jensen-huang-to-testify-before-congress-live-latest-updates">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Who could replace the departed Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO?</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/12/jensen-huang-nvidia-ceo-replacement</link>
      <description><p>Chief financial officer Colette Kress to take over on interim basis but other names are in mix to be permanent successor</p><p>The hunt is on for a new Nvidia CEO. It comes after a whirlwind week, which saw the company head and co-founder, Jensen Huang, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/12/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-resigns">resign amid multiple allegations of extramarital affairs</a>, including one that involved an alleged Chinese spy and two with company employees.</p><p>Nvidia immediately named Colette Kress, the company’s chief financial officer, as the interim CEO. It’s possible she could stay on permanently, but the company could also name another candidate for the full-time role.
